covered.grounds: The file ends at the closing brace (run.py:356-360). Not EQUIVALENT: its bytes differ, so its entry in the manifest (run.py:298-302, a sha of the raw bytes) and the anchor value (run.py:313-315) differ for the same inputs. Nothing compares that value with one from another execution (the file also holds `started: clock()`, so the bytes are never reproducible across executions anyway): verify recomputes the manifest from the same bytes (verify.py:117-124) and every code reader json.loads the text. Completeness of this file is decided by parse, not by a trailing newline (one write call, then flush and fsync; a cut file does not parse, and a file cut after the brace is a whole JSON document either way).
